en.B: Once more Jesus answered them by speaking in parables:
en.R: Jesus answered them again by telling stories. He told this one:

es.B: Jesús volvió a responderles hablando en parábolas:
es.R: Jesús les respondió otra vez contándoles historias. Les contó esta:

fr.L: Et, prenant la parole, Jésus leur parla de nouveau en paraboles, disant :
fr.B: Une fois de plus, Jésus leur répondit en leur parlant en paraboles :
fr.R: Jésus leur a encore répondu en racontant des histoires. Il leur a raconté celle-ci :

sw.L: Na akijibu, Yesu tena alisema nao kwa mifano, akisema:
sw.B: Yesu aliwajibu tena kwa kusema nao kwa mifano:
sw.R: Yesu aliwajibu tena kwa kuwasimulia hadithi. Akawasimulia hadithi hii:

vi.B: Đức Giê-xu lại dùng ngụ ngôn mà đáp lời họ:
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu lại trả lời họ bằng những câu chuyện. Ngài kể chuyện này:

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 대답하여 다시 비유로 그들에게 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 다시 비유로 그들에게 대답하셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 다시 비유, 곧 무엇에 빗대어 하는 이야기로 그들에게 대답하셨다. 예수께서 이런 이야기를 들려주셨다.

pt.B: Mais uma vez Jesus lhes respondeu falando em parábolas:
pt.R: Jesus respondeu a eles outra vez contando histórias. Ele contou esta:

am.L: ኢየሱስም መልሶ እንደገና በምሳሌዎች ተናገራቸው፤ እንዲህም አለ፦
am.B: ኢየሱስ እንደገና በምሳሌዎች ተናግሮ መለሰላቸው፦
am.R: ኢየሱስ ታሪኮችን በመንገር እንደገና መለሰላቸው። ይህንንም ነገራቸው፦

decisions.choice: answering: responding to the situation, the leaders' wish to arrest him (21:45-46)
decisions.reason: No one has asked a question. The word often means simply "spoke up" in reply to what had happened.

decisions.choice: in parables: by way of parables, the manner of his teaching
decisions.reason: Only one parable follows. The plural describes how he taught, as in 13:3 and 22:1.

decisions.choice: telling stories; He told this one
decisions.reason: Readable says what parables are and introduces the one story that follows.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal; speech keeps its own tenses at every level
decisions.reason: As in John, Mark and Luke, and in Matthew 11: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading, while Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers now meet stories. This holds for the whole passage, including 22:15-22.

decisions.choice: mifano (L, B); hadithi (R)
decisions.reason: "Mfano" is the Swahili word for a parable, a story that compares; "methali" is a proverb. Readable says "stories", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 22:1-22; "그분" (L), "예수" (B, R) in the narrative; historic presents kept only at Literal
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters; respect for Jesus is carried by -시- and 께서 (style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "비유" explained once at Readable
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 12:1: Readable keeps the word and says what a parable is.

decisions.choice: "ngụ ngôn" (L, B); "câu chuyện" (R) for parables
decisions.reason: As settled for the Gospels and in 21:33; the narrator still calls Jesus "Ngài" and his speaking "nói".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic
alternatives: a span on every pronoun for God or Jesus, as in English
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Christ has nothing to change in Amharic. This holds through the passage.

source.text: Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ, ὅστις ἐποίησεν γάμους τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Has become like the kingdom of the heavens to a man, a king, who made a wedding feast for the son of him.

en.L: "The kingdom of the heavens has become like a man, a king, who made a wedding feast for his son.
en.B: "What happens in the kingdom of heaven can be compared to this: a king prepared a wedding banquet for his son.
en.R: "The kingdom of heaven is like this. A king gave a big wedding party for his son.

es.L: «Ha llegado a ser semejante el reino de los cielos a un hombre, un rey, que hizo una fiesta de bodas para su hijo.
es.B: «Lo que sucede en el reino de los cielos se puede comparar con esto: un rey preparó un banquete de bodas para su hijo.
es.R: «El reino de los cielos es así: un rey hizo una gran fiesta de bodas para su hijo.

fr.L: « Le royaume des cieux est devenu semblable à un homme, un roi, qui a fait un festin de noces pour son fils.
fr.B: « Voici à quoi l’on peut comparer ce qui se passe dans le royaume des cieux : un roi a préparé un banquet de noces pour son fils.
fr.R: « Le royaume des cieux ressemble à ceci. Un roi a organisé une grande fête de mariage pour son fils.

sw.L: "Ufalme wa mbinguni umekuwa kama mtu, mfalme, aliyemfanyia mwana wake karamu ya arusi.
sw.B: "Yanayotokea katika ufalme wa mbinguni yanaweza kulinganishwa na hili: mfalme mmoja aliandaa karamu ya arusi ya mwana wake.
sw.R: "Ufalme wa mbinguni uko hivi: mfalme mmoja alimfanyia mwanawe sherehe kubwa ya arusi.

vi.L: "Vương quốc thiên đàng được ví như một người kia, là một vị vua, đã làm tiệc cưới cho con trai mình.
vi.B: "Vương quốc thiên đàng giống như chuyện một vị vua kia làm tiệc cưới cho con trai mình.
vi.R: "Vương quốc thiên đàng giống như chuyện sau đây. Có một vị vua tổ chức một bữa tiệc cưới lớn cho con trai mình.

ko.L: "천국은 자기 아들을 위하여 혼인 잔치를 베푼 어떤 사람, 곧 왕에게 비유되었다.
ko.B: "천국은 자기 아들의 혼인 잔치를 베푼 어떤 왕의 이야기와 같다.
ko.R: "천국은 이런 일과 같다. 어떤 왕이 자기 아들의 결혼을 축하하려고 큰 잔치를 열었다.

pt.L: "O Reino dos céus se tornou semelhante a um homem, um rei, que fez uma festa de casamento para o seu filho.
pt.B: "O que acontece no Reino dos céus pode ser comparado a isto: um rei preparou um banquete de casamento para o seu filho.
pt.R: "O Reino dos céus é como esta história. Um rei deu uma grande festa de casamento para o seu filho.

am.L: «መንግሥተ ሰማያት ለልጁ ሰርግ ያደረገን ንጉሥ የሆነ ሰው መሰለች።
am.B: «በመንግሥተ ሰማያት የሚሆነው ነገር እንዲህ ሊመሰል ይችላል፤ አንድ ንጉሥ ለልጁ የሰርግ ግብዣ አዘጋጀ።
am.R: «የሰማይ መንግሥት እንዲህ ናት። አንድ ንጉሥ ለልጁ ትልቅ የሰርግ ድግስ አደረገ።

decisions.choice: has become like: the kingdom is compared to the whole story that follows
alternatives: the kingdom is like the king himself
decisions.reason: The same form begins the parables of 13:24 and 18:23. The point lies in the events of the story, not in the king alone.

decisions.choice: wedding feast: the celebration of a marriage, which could last several days
decisions.reason: The plural word names the wedding festivities. A king's feast for his son was the greatest celebration a city could see.

decisions.choice: the king and his son: God and Jesus, as in the vineyard owner's son (21:37)
alternatives: a story with no figure for God
decisions.reason: The prophets picture God's coming rule as a feast (Isaiah 25:6), and Jesus has just told of a father who sent his son (21:37). The parable's figures still remain figures in a story.

decisions.choice: a man, a king
decisions.reason: The Greek says "a man, a king", a common way of introducing a character. Balanced and Readable say "a king".

decisions.choice: his son: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The king is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no span, as with the bridegroom in 9:15.

decisions.choice: el reino de los cielos, at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of Matthew's phrase. Spanish keeps the plural "cielos" of the Greek, and Readable keeps the phrase as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: the parable in the passé composé at every level (22:2-14)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The parable is Jesus's speech, and French speech tells past events in the passé composé, as in the parables of Mark 4. Literal still keeps the Greek present of narration inside the story ("il dit", 22:8 and 22:12).

decisions.choice: un festin de noces (L); un banquet de noces (B); une grande fête de mariage (R)
decisions.reason: The word here means the feast that celebrated the marriage (m2), so French names the meal. "Noces" alone sounds literary, as John 2:1 notes, but it is current in the set phrases "festin de noces" and "habit de noces"; Readable uses everyday words.

decisions.choice: ufalme wa mbinguni, at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of Matthew's phrase: the locative "mbinguni" (in heaven) is how Swahili says "of the heavens" naturally; "ufalme wa mbingu" sounds like a kingdom made of the skies.

decisions.choice: "천국" at every level; "어떤 사람, 곧 왕에게 비유되었다" (L); "왕의 이야기와 같다" (B); "이런 일과 같다" (R)
decisions.reason: The kingdom is compared to the whole story (meaning decision); the wording follows the Korean Matthew 18:23.

decisions.choice: "혼인 잔치" (L, B); "결혼을 축하하는 큰 잔치" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Matthew 9:15: the feast, not the ceremony.

decisions.choice: "vương quốc thiên đàng" at every level; "được ví như" (L), "giống như chuyện" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As settled for Matthew and in 18:23: the kingdom is compared to the whole story that follows (meaning decision), not to the king alone.

decisions.choice: "vua" and "con trai mình" with no deity_pronoun span (whole parable)
alternatives: a span on the king's pronouns
decisions.reason: As in 18:23-35: a king in a parable is a figure in the story, so he is "vua" or "ông", and he says "ta" in lowercase.

decisions.choice: "መንግሥተ ሰማያት" (L, B); "የሰማይ መንግሥት" (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term for Matthew's kingdom of heaven: the Ge'ez phrase is the living church word at Literal and Balanced, and Readable uses the plain Amharic phrase. The same holds through this passage.

source.text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ καλέσαι τοὺς κεκλημένους εἰς τοὺς γάμους, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελον ἐλθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And he sent the slaves of him to call those having been invited to the wedding feast, and not they were willing to come.

en.L: And he sent his slaves to call those who had been invited to the wedding feast, and they were not willing to come.
en.B: He sent his servants to summon the guests who had already been invited, but they refused to come.
en.R: He sent his servants to tell the invited guests to come to the party. But they would not come.

es.L: Y envió a sus esclavos a llamar a los que habían sido invitados a la fiesta de bodas, y no querían venir.
es.B: Envió a sus siervos a llamar a los que ya estaban invitados, pero se negaron a venir.
es.R: Mandó a sus siervos a decirles a los invitados que vinieran a la fiesta. Pero ellos no quisieron venir.

fr.L: Et il a envoyé ses esclaves appeler ceux qui avaient été invités aux noces, et ils ne voulaient pas venir.
fr.B: Il a envoyé ses serviteurs appeler ceux qu’il avait déjà invités, mais ils ont refusé de venir.
fr.R: Il a envoyé ses serviteurs dire aux invités de venir à la fête. Mais ils ne voulaient pas venir.

sw.L: Na aliwatuma watumwa wake kuwaita wale waliokuwa wamealikwa kwenye karamu ya arusi, nao hawakutaka kuja.
sw.B: Aliwatuma watumishi wake kuwaita wageni waliokuwa wamekwisha kualikwa, lakini walikataa kuja.
sw.R: Aliwatuma watumishi wake kuwaambia wageni walioalikwa waje kwenye sherehe. Lakini wao hawakutaka kuja.

vi.L: Và vua sai các nô lệ của mình đi gọi những người đã được mời đến dự tiệc cưới, nhưng họ không muốn đến.
vi.B: Vua sai các đầy tớ đi gọi những khách đã được mời đến dự tiệc, nhưng họ không chịu đến.
vi.R: Vua sai các đầy tớ đi báo cho những khách đã được mời rằng đã đến giờ dự tiệc. Nhưng họ không chịu đến.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 혼인 잔치에 초대받은 사람들을 부르러 자기 종들을 보냈다. 그러나 그들은 오려고 하지 않았다.
ko.B: 왕은 혼인 잔치에 초대받은 손님들을 불러오라고 종들을 보냈다. 그러나 그들은 오려고 하지 않았다.
ko.R: 왕은 초대한 손님들에게 이제 잔치에 오라고 전하려고 종들을 보냈다. 그러나 그들은 오지 않으려고 했다.

pt.L: E enviou os seus escravos para chamar os convidados para a festa de casamento, e eles não quiseram vir.
pt.B: Ele enviou os seus servos para chamar os que já tinham sido convidados, mas eles se recusaram a vir.
pt.R: Ele mandou os seus servos dizerem aos convidados que viessem para a festa. Mas eles não quiseram vir.

am.L: የተጠሩትንም ወደ ሰርጉ ይጠሩ ዘንድ ባሪያዎቹን ላከ፤ ሊመጡም አልፈለጉም።
am.B: ቀድሞ የተጋበዙትን እንግዶች እንዲጠሩ ባሪያዎቹን ላከ፤ እነርሱ ግን ለመምጣት እምቢ አሉ።
am.R: የተጋበዙት እንግዶች ወደ ግብዣው እንዲመጡ እንዲነግሯቸው ባሪያዎቹን ላከ። እነርሱ ግን ሊመጡ አልፈለጉም።

decisions.choice: two invitations: one sent ahead of time, then a call when the feast was ready
alternatives: a first invitation on the day
decisions.reason: Guests were invited in advance and then summoned when the meal was ready (compare Esther 5:8; 6:14). These guests had already accepted the first invitation.

decisions.choice: slaves: persons owned by the king and sent on his business
decisions.reason: The word names a slave (8:9; 10:24). A king's slaves could carry his messages with his authority.

decisions.choice: the slaves sent: God's messengers to Israel
decisions.reason: As in the parable of the tenants (21:34-36), the slaves sent and mistreated recall the prophets God sent to his people (23:34-37).

decisions.choice: they were not willing: they kept refusing
decisions.reason: The verb means to want or be willing. The guests chose not to come.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclavos (L); siervos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering, as the English has slaves (L) and servants (B, R): Literal keeps that the men were owned (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable use the word for a king's servants. The same through verse 10.

decisions.choice: esclaves (L); serviteurs (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's forms, as the English: Literal keeps "esclave" and the meaning decision (m2) keeps that they were owned. The same for 22:4-10. "Ils ne voulaient pas" at Literal and Readable keeps the repeated refusal of the imperfect (m4).

decisions.choice: watumwa (L); watumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering, as the English has slaves (L) and servants (B, R): Literal keeps that the men were owned (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable use the word for a king's servants. The same through verse 10.

decisions.choice: "종" at every level for doulos, through this parable
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 12:2 and Matthew 18:23-35: Korean "종" already means one owned and sent by a master.

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" (L); "đầy tớ" (B, R) for doulos (whole parable)
decisions.reason: As settled in Matthew 10:24 and 18:23 and for doulos throughout.

decisions.choice: "đã đến giờ dự tiệc" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision describes two invitations, the second a call when the feast was ready; Readable says so, since the plain reader would not know the custom.

decisions.choice: "የተጠሩት ... ይጠሩ" (L); "የተጋበዙ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses one verb for invite and call, and the parable ends on it (22:14, "many are called"); Amharic "መጥራት" also means both, so Literal keeps the repetition. Balanced and Readable say "invited" plainly.

decisions.choice: "ባሪያዎች" at Balanced and Readable too
alternatives: "አገልጋዮች" (servants), as the English Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "ባሪያ" for the Greek word at every level; "አገልጋዮች" is kept for the different word in 22:13.

source.text: πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους λέγων· Εἴπατε τοῖς κεκλημένοις· Ἰδοὺ τὸ ἄριστόν μου ἡτοίμακα, οἱ ταῦροί μου καὶ τὰ σιτιστὰ τεθυμένα, καὶ πάντα ἕτοιμα· δεῦτε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.

records.literal_gloss: Again he sent other slaves, saying, Say to those having been invited, Behold, the dinner of me I have prepared, the oxen of me and the fatlings having been slaughtered, and all things ready; come to the wedding feast.

en.L: Again he sent other slaves, saying, 'Tell those who have been invited, "Look, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and fattened animals have been slaughtered, and everything [is] ready. Come to the wedding feast."'
en.B: So he sent more servants with this message: 'Tell the guests, "See, my banquet is prepared. My bulls and my fattened calves have been slaughtered. Everything is ready, so come to the wedding."'
en.R: Then the king sent some other servants. He told them, 'Say to the guests, "The meal is ready! I have killed my best cattle for the food. Everything is ready. Come to the wedding party!"'

es.L: De nuevo envió a otros esclavos, diciendo: “{{plural_you:Digan|Decid}} a los invitados: ‘{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, he preparado mi comida; mis toros y las reses cebadas han sido sacrificados, y todo [está] listo; {{plural_you:vengan|venid}} a la fiesta de bodas’”.
es.B: Entonces envió a otros siervos con este mensaje: “{{plural_you:Digan|Decid}} a los invitados: ‘{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, mi banquete está preparado. Mis toros y mis terneros cebados ya están sacrificados. Todo está listo; {{plural_you:vengan|venid}} a la boda’”.
es.R: Luego el rey mandó a otros siervos. Les dijo: “{{plural_you:Díganles|Decidles}} a los invitados: ‘¡La comida está lista! He matado mis mejores reses para el banquete. Todo está preparado. ¡{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} a la fiesta de bodas!’”.

fr.L: De nouveau il a envoyé d’autres esclaves, disant : “Dites à ceux qui ont été invités : ‹ Voici, j’ai préparé mon déjeuner ; mes taureaux et mes bêtes engraissées ont été égorgés, et tout [est] prêt ; venez aux noces. › ”
fr.B: Il a donc envoyé d’autres serviteurs avec ce message : “Dites aux invités : ‹ Voyez, mon banquet est prêt. Mes taureaux et mes veaux gras ont été abattus. Tout est prêt : venez aux noces. › ”
fr.R: Alors le roi a envoyé d’autres serviteurs. Il leur a dit : “Dites aux invités : ‹ Le repas est prêt ! J’ai fait tuer mes meilleurs bœufs pour le repas. Tout est prêt. Venez à la fête de mariage ! › ”

sw.L: Tena aliwatuma watumwa wengine, akisema, 'Waambieni walioalikwa, "Angalieni, nimekwisha kutayarisha chakula changu; mafahali wangu na wanyama walionenepeshwa wamechinjwa, na kila kitu [kiko] tayari. Njooni kwenye karamu ya arusi."'
sw.B: Akatuma tena watumishi wengine na ujumbe huu: 'Waambieni walioalikwa, "Tazameni, karamu yangu iko tayari. Mafahali wangu na ndama wangu walionona wamechinjwa. Kila kitu kiko tayari, basi njooni arusini."'
sw.R: Kisha mfalme akatuma watumishi wengine. Aliwaambia, 'Waambieni wageni, "Chakula kiko tayari! Nimechinja ng'ombe wangu bora kwa ajili ya karamu. Kila kitu kiko tayari. Njooni kwenye sherehe ya arusi!"'

vi.L: Vua lại sai các nô lệ khác, nói rằng: 'Hãy nói với những người đã được mời: "Này, ta đã dọn tiệc của ta rồi; bò đực và thú vật béo của ta đã làm thịt, và mọi thứ đều sẵn sàng. Hãy đến dự tiệc cưới."'
vi.B: Vua lại sai những đầy tớ khác đi và dặn: 'Hãy nói với các khách được mời: "Kìa, tiệc của ta đã dọn xong. Bò đực và bê béo của ta đã làm thịt. Mọi thứ đều đã sẵn sàng. Mời đến dự tiệc cưới!"'
vi.R: Rồi vua sai những đầy tớ khác đi. Vua dặn họ: 'Hãy nói với các khách được mời: "Bữa tiệc đã sẵn sàng! Ta đã làm thịt những con bò ngon nhất để đãi khách. Mọi thứ đều đã sẵn sàng. Mời đến dự tiệc cưới!"'

ko.L: 다시 그는 다른 종들을 보내며 말했다. '초대받은 사람들에게 말하여라. "보라, 내가 내 식사를 준비하였다. 내 소들과 살진 짐승들을 잡았고, 모든 것이 준비되었다. 혼인 잔치에 오너라."'
ko.B: 왕은 다시 다른 종들을 보내며 일렀다. '초대받은 사람들에게 이렇게 전하여라. "보십시오, 내가 잔치 음식을 다 차렸습니다. 황소와 살진 송아지를 잡았고 모든 것이 준비되었으니, 혼인 잔치에 오십시오."'
ko.R: 그러자 왕은 다른 종들을 보내며 말했다. '손님들에게 가서 이렇게 말하여라. "음식이 다 준비되었습니다! 제일 좋은 소들을 잡아 음식을 만들었습니다. 모든 것이 다 준비되었으니, 결혼 잔치에 오십시오!"'

pt.L: De novo enviou outros escravos, dizendo: 'Digam aos convidados: "Vejam, preparei a minha refeição; os meus bois e os animais cevados foram abatidos, e tudo [está] pronto. Venham para a festa de casamento."'
pt.B: Então ele enviou mais servos com esta mensagem: 'Digam aos convidados: "Vejam, o meu banquete está preparado. Os meus touros e os meus bezerros cevados foram abatidos. Tudo está pronto; venham para o casamento."'
pt.R: Então o rei mandou outros servos. Ele disse a eles: 'Digam aos convidados: "A comida está pronta! Matei o meu melhor gado para a festa. Tudo está pronto. Venham para a festa de casamento!"'

am.L: ደግሞም ሌሎች ባሪያዎችን እንዲህ ብሎ ላከ፦ “የተጠሩትን እንዲህ በሏቸው፦ ‘እነሆ፣ ምሳዬን አዘጋጅቻለሁ፤ ኮርማዎቼና የሰቡ እንስሶቼ ታርደዋል፤ ሁሉም [ነገር] ተዘጋጅቷል፤ ወደ ሰርጉ ኑ።’”
am.B: ስለዚህ ሌሎች ባሪያዎችን እንዲህ ብሎ ላከ፦ “እንግዶቹን እንዲህ በሏቸው፦ ‘እነሆ፣ ግብዣዬ ተዘጋጅቷል። ኮርማዎቼና የሰቡ ጥጆቼ ታርደዋል። ሁሉም ነገር ተዘጋጅቷልና ወደ ሰርጉ ኑ።’”
am.R: ከዚያም ንጉሡ ሌሎች ባሪያዎችን ላከ። እንዲህም አላቸው፦ “እንግዶቹን እንዲህ በሏቸው፦ ‘ምግቡ ተዘጋጅቷል! ለግብዣው ምርጥ ከብቶቼን አርጃለሁ። ሁሉም ነገር ተዘጋጅቷል። ወደ ሰርጉ ድግስ ኑ!’”

decisions.choice: dinner: the first meal of the feast, eaten about midday
decisions.reason: The word names the morning or midday meal. Here it opens the wedding celebration.

decisions.choice: oxen and fattened animals: a lavish feast
decisions.reason: Meat was rare for most people. Slaughtering oxen and stall-fed animals showed a royal feast with no expense spared.

decisions.choice: look (L); see (B); not rendered (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable names the king so the reader keeps track of who is speaking.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" (Digan|Decid, vengan|venid)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: mon déjeuner (L); mon banquet (B); le repas (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the first meal of the feast, eaten about midday (m1), which is what French "déjeuner" means; English "dinner" would be "dîner", an evening meal. Balanced and Readable name the feast, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ‹ › for the message inside the king's words, inside Jesus's
decisions.reason: French marks a third level of quotation with single guillemets ‹ ›, as in Mark 12:36: « » are Jesus's words, “ ” the king's, and ‹ › what the servants are to say.

decisions.choice: "보라" (L); "보십시오" (B); not rendered (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Matthew's "behold" as "보라", as in the Korean Matthew; at Balanced it belongs to a polite message, so it takes the message's speech level.

decisions.choice: The king's message to the guests in 합쇼체 (B, R); the plain style at Literal
alternatives: the plain style at every level
decisions.reason: A king inviting honoured guests speaks courteously; Literal keeps the bare imperative of the Greek.

decisions.choice: the king says "ta" in lowercase with no span, and speaks to his servants with commands
decisions.reason: A king speaking in a parable, as in 18:32; "ta" is the word of one in authority and takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: ‘ ’ for the message inside the king's words
decisions.reason: The king's words are already inside Jesus's « » and take “ ”; the message he sends is a third level, marked ‘ ’ as the Spanish does, so the marks still pair.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀμελήσαντες ἀπῆλθον, ὃς μὲν εἰς τὸν ἴδιον ἀγρόν, ὃς δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ἐμπορίαν αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: But having paid no attention, they went away, one to the own field, another to the business of him;

en.L: But paying no attention, they went off, one to his own field, another to his business.
en.B: The guests did not care. They went off, one to his farm and another to his trade.
en.R: But the guests did not care. One went off to work in his field. Another went to his business.

es.L: Pero ellos, sin hacer caso, se fueron, uno a su propio campo, otro a su negocio.
es.B: Los invitados no hicieron caso. Se fueron, uno a su finca y otro a su negocio.
es.R: Pero a los invitados no les importó. Uno se fue a trabajar en su campo. Otro se fue a su negocio.

fr.L: Mais eux, n’en ayant pas tenu compte, s’en sont allés, l’un à son propre champ, l’autre à son commerce.
fr.B: Les invités ne s’en sont pas souciés. Ils s’en sont allés, l’un à sa ferme, l’autre à son commerce.
fr.R: Mais les invités ne s’y sont pas intéressés. L’un est parti travailler dans son champ. Un autre est allé à ses affaires.

sw.L: Lakini wao, wakipuuza, waliondoka, mmoja kwenda shamba lake mwenyewe, mwingine kwenda kwenye biashara yake.
sw.B: Wageni hao hawakulijali jambo hilo. Waliondoka, mmoja akaenda kwenye shamba lake, mwingine kwenye shughuli zake za biashara.
sw.R: Lakini wageni hawakujali. Mmoja aliondoka kwenda kufanya kazi shambani mwake. Mwingine akaenda kwenye biashara yake.

vi.L: Nhưng họ chẳng màng đến, bỏ đi, người thì về ruộng mình, người thì đi buôn bán.
vi.B: Nhưng các khách được mời chẳng quan tâm. Họ bỏ đi, người thì ra đồng ruộng, người thì lo việc buôn bán.
vi.R: Nhưng các khách ấy không thèm để ý. Một người đi làm ngoài ruộng của mình. Một người khác đi lo việc buôn bán.

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 무시하고 떠나갔다. 어떤 사람은 자기 밭으로, 어떤 사람은 자기 장사하러 [갔다].
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 그 말을 대수롭지 않게 여기고 가 버렸다. 한 사람은 자기 밭으로, 또 한 사람은 장사하러 갔다.
ko.R: 그러나 손님들은 신경도 쓰지 않았다. 한 사람은 자기 밭에 일하러 갔다. 또 한 사람은 장사하러 갔다.

pt.L: Mas eles, sem dar importância, foram embora, um para o seu próprio campo, outro para o seu negócio.
pt.B: Os convidados não deram importância. Foram embora, um para o seu sítio e outro para o seu comércio.
pt.R: Mas os convidados não se importaram. Um foi trabalhar no seu campo. Outro foi cuidar do seu negócio.

am.L: እነርሱ ግን ቸል ብለው ሄዱ፤ አንዱ ወደ ገዛ እርሻው፣ ሌላውም ወደ ንግዱ፤
am.B: እንግዶቹ ግን ግድ አልሰጣቸውም። አንዱ ወደ እርሻው፣ ሌላውም ወደ ንግዱ ሄደ።
am.R: እንግዶቹ ግን ግድ አልሰጣቸውም። አንዱ በእርሻው ሊሠራ ሄደ። ሌላው ወደ ንግዱ ሄደ።

decisions.choice: paying no attention: treating the invitation as unimportant
decisions.reason: The verb means to neglect or make light of something. They heard and did not care.

decisions.choice: business: trade, buying and selling
decisions.reason: The word names commerce. Ordinary work mattered more to them than the king's feast.

decisions.choice: the guests
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who went off.

decisions.choice: [갔다]
decisions.reason: Korean needs the verb the Greek leaves understood.

source.text: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ κρατήσαντες τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὕβρισαν καὶ ἀπέκτειναν.

records.literal_gloss: And the rest, having seized the slaves of him, mistreated and killed [them].

en.L: And the rest seized his slaves, mistreated [them], and killed [them].
en.B: The rest laid hands on the king's servants, abused them, and killed them.
en.R: The rest of the guests grabbed the king's servants. They hurt them and killed them.

es.L: Y los demás, apoderándose de sus esclavos, [los] maltrataron y [los] mataron.
es.B: Los demás agarraron a los siervos del rey, los maltrataron y los mataron.
es.R: Los demás invitados agarraron a los siervos del rey. Los trataron mal y los mataron.

fr.L: Et les autres, ayant saisi ses esclaves, [les] ont outragés et [les] ont tués.
fr.B: Les autres se sont emparés des serviteurs du roi, les ont maltraités et les ont tués.
fr.R: Les autres invités ont attrapé les serviteurs du roi. Ils les ont frappés et ils les ont tués.

sw.L: Na waliobaki, wakiwashika watumwa wake, waliwadhalilisha na kuwaua.
sw.B: Waliobaki waliwakamata watumishi wa mfalme, wakawadhalilisha, kisha wakawaua.
sw.R: Wageni wengine waliwakamata watumishi wa mfalme. Waliwaumiza na kuwaua.

vi.L: Còn những người khác bắt các nô lệ của vua, sỉ nhục và giết đi.
vi.B: Những người còn lại bắt các đầy tớ của vua, hành hạ rồi giết đi.
vi.R: Những khách còn lại bắt các đầy tớ của vua. Họ đánh đập và giết chết các đầy tớ ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 나머지 사람들은 그의 종들을 붙잡아 모욕하고 죽였다.
ko.B: 나머지 사람들은 왕의 종들을 붙잡아 모욕하고 죽였다.
ko.R: 나머지 손님들은 왕의 종들을 붙잡았다. 그리고 그들을 때리고 죽였다.

pt.L: E os demais, agarrando os escravos dele, [os] maltrataram e [os] mataram.
pt.B: Os outros agarraram os servos do rei, os humilharam e os mataram.
pt.R: Os outros convidados agarraram os servos do rei. Eles machucaram os servos e os mataram.

am.L: የቀሩትም ባሪያዎቹን ይዘው አንገላቷቸው፤ ገደሏቸውም።
am.B: የቀሩት ደግሞ የንጉሡን ባሪያዎች ይዘው አዋረዷቸው፤ ገደሏቸውም።
am.R: ከእንግዶቹ የቀሩት የንጉሡን ባሪያዎች ያዙ። አቆሰሏቸው፤ ገደሏቸውም።

decisions.choice: mistreated: treated with insult and violence
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat someone with outrage and contempt. It can include beating.

decisions.choice: the slaves killed: as the tenants did in 21:35-36
alternatives: a new detail with no echo
decisions.reason: The parable repeats the pattern of the vineyard story and of Israel's treatment of the prophets (23:37).

decisions.choice: the king's; of the guests (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear whose servants these were and who the rest were.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: "sỉ nhục và giết đi" (L) with no brackets
decisions.reason: Vietnamese, like the Greek, can leave the object unstated when the sentence makes it plain, as in Mark 12:3, so the English bracketed "[them]" has nothing to supply.

source.text: ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς ὠργίσθη, καὶ πέμψας τὰ στρατεύματα αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεσεν τοὺς φονεῖς ἐκείνους καὶ τὴν πόλιν αὐτῶν ἐνέπρησεν.

records.literal_gloss: The and king was angry, and having sent the armies of him he destroyed the murderers those and the city of them burned.

en.L: But the king was angry, and sending his armies he destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
en.B: The king was furious. He sent his troops, wiped out those murderers, and set their city on fire.
en.R: The king became very angry. He sent his soldiers to kill those murderers and burn down their city.

es.L: Pero el rey se enojó, y enviando sus tropas, destruyó a aquellos asesinos y la ciudad de ellos incendió.
es.B: El rey se enfureció. Envió a sus tropas, acabó con aquellos asesinos y prendió fuego a su ciudad.
es.R: El rey se enojó muchísimo. Mandó a sus soldados a matar a aquellos asesinos y a quemar su ciudad.

fr.L: Mais le roi s’est mis en colère, et, ayant envoyé ses armées, il a fait périr ces meurtriers-là et a incendié leur ville.
fr.B: Le roi est entré dans une violente colère. Il a envoyé ses troupes, il a exterminé ces meurtriers et il a mis le feu à leur ville.
fr.R: Le roi s’est mis très en colère. Il a envoyé ses soldats pour tuer ces meurtriers et brûler leur ville.

sw.L: Lakini mfalme alikasirika, na akiyatuma majeshi yake, aliwaangamiza wauaji wale na kuuteketeza mji wao.
sw.B: Mfalme alikasirika mno. Akatuma vikosi vyake vya askari, akawaangamiza wauaji hao, akauteketeza mji wao kwa moto.
sw.R: Mfalme alikasirika sana. Aliwatuma askari wake kuwaua wauaji hao na kuuchoma moto mji wao.

vi.L: Vua nổi giận, và sai quân đội của mình tiêu diệt những kẻ giết người ấy và đốt thành của chúng.
vi.B: Vua vô cùng tức giận. Vua sai quân lính đến tiêu diệt bọn sát nhân ấy và đốt cháy thành của chúng.
vi.R: Vua rất tức giận. Vua sai quân lính đến giết bọn giết người ấy và đốt cháy thành của chúng.

ko.L: 그러자 왕이 노하여, 자기 군대를 보내어 그 살인자들을 멸망시키고 그들의 도시를 불살랐다.
ko.B: 왕은 몹시 화가 나서 군대를 보내어 그 살인자들을 없애고 그들의 도시를 불태웠다.
ko.R: 왕은 크게 화가 났다. 그래서 군인들을 보내어 그 살인자들을 죽이고 그들의 도시를 불태워 버렸다.

pt.L: Mas o rei ficou irado e, enviando os seus exércitos, destruiu aqueles assassinos e incendiou a cidade deles.
pt.B: O rei ficou furioso. Enviou as suas tropas, acabou com aqueles assassinos e pôs fogo na cidade deles.
pt.R: O rei ficou muito bravo. Ele mandou os seus soldados matarem aqueles assassinos e queimarem a cidade deles.

am.L: ንጉሡም ተቆጣ፤ ሠራዊቱንም ልኮ እነዚያን ነፍሰ ገዳዮች አጠፋ፤ ከተማቸውንም አቃጠለ።
am.B: ንጉሡ እጅግ ተቆጣ። ወታደሮቹን ልኮ እነዚያን ነፍሰ ገዳዮች አጠፋቸው፤ ከተማቸውንም በእሳት አቃጠለ።
am.R: ንጉሡ በጣም ተናደደ። እነዚያን ነፍሰ ገዳዮች እንዲገድሉና ከተማቸውን እንዲያቃጥሉ ወታደሮቹን ላከ።

decisions.choice: armies: troops, soldiers
decisions.reason: The plural word means bodies of soldiers.

decisions.choice: burned their city: the judgment that falls on those who refused the king
alternatives: a direct prediction of the fall of Jerusalem in AD 70
decisions.reason: Burning a rebel city was a common act of war and a picture the prophets use for judgment (Isaiah 1:7). Many readers see a pointer to the destruction of Jerusalem (compare 23:38; 24:2); the parable does not name the city.

decisions.choice: "chúng" for the murderers
decisions.reason: Vietnamese pronouns show attitude: once the guests have killed the king's servants, the narrator speaks of them as "chúng", as of the wicked in 13:41.

source.text: τότε λέγει τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ· Ὁ μὲν γάμος ἕτοιμός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ κεκλημένοι οὐκ ἦσαν ἄξιοι·

records.literal_gloss: Then he says to the slaves of him, The indeed wedding feast ready is, but those having been invited were not worthy;

en.L: Then he says to his slaves, 'The wedding feast is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy.
en.B: Then he told his servants, 'The wedding is ready, but the guests I invited did not deserve to come.
en.R: Then the king said to his servants, 'The wedding party is ready. But the people I invited did not deserve to come.

es.L: Entonces dice a sus esclavos: “La fiesta de bodas está lista, pero los que habían sido invitados no eran dignos.
es.B: Luego dijo a sus siervos: “La boda está preparada, pero los que invité no merecían venir.
es.R: Entonces el rey les dijo a sus siervos: “La fiesta de bodas está lista. Pero los que invité no merecían venir.

fr.L: Alors il dit à ses esclaves : “Le festin de noces est prêt, mais ceux qui avaient été invités n’en étaient pas dignes.
fr.B: Puis il a dit à ses serviteurs : “Le banquet de noces est prêt, mais ceux que j’avais invités ne méritaient pas d’y venir.
fr.R: Ensuite, le roi a dit à ses serviteurs : “La fête de mariage est prête. Mais les gens que j’avais invités ne méritaient pas de venir.

sw.L: Kisha anawaambia watumwa wake, 'Karamu ya arusi iko tayari, lakini walioalikwa hawakustahili.
sw.B: Kisha aliwaambia watumishi wake, 'Arusi iko tayari, lakini wale niliowaalika hawakustahili kuja.
sw.R: Kisha mfalme akawaambia watumishi wake, 'Sherehe ya arusi iko tayari. Lakini watu niliowaalika hawakustahili kuja.

vi.L: Bấy giờ vua nói với các nô lệ của mình: 'Tiệc cưới đã sẵn sàng, nhưng những người được mời không xứng đáng.
vi.B: Bấy giờ vua bảo các đầy tớ: 'Tiệc cưới đã sẵn sàng, nhưng những khách ta mời không xứng đáng dự.
vi.R: Rồi vua nói với các đầy tớ: 'Tiệc cưới đã sẵn sàng. Nhưng những người mà ta mời không đáng được đến dự.

ko.L: 그때에 그가 자기 종들에게 말한다. '혼인 잔치는 준비되었으나, 초대받은 사람들은 합당하지 않았다.
ko.B: 그러고 나서 왕은 종들에게 말했다. '혼인 잔치는 준비되었는데, 초대받은 사람들은 올 자격이 없었다.
ko.R: 그다음에 왕이 종들에게 말했다. '결혼 잔치는 다 준비되었다. 그런데 내가 초대한 사람들은 올 자격이 없었다.

pt.L: Então diz aos seus escravos: 'A festa de casamento está pronta, mas os convidados não eram dignos.
pt.B: Então ele disse aos seus servos: 'O casamento está pronto, mas os convidados que eu chamei não mereciam vir.
pt.R: Então o rei disse aos seus servos: 'A festa de casamento está pronta. Mas as pessoas que eu convidei não mereciam vir.

am.L: ከዚያም ባሪያዎቹን ይላቸዋል፦ “ሰርጉ ተዘጋጅቷል፤ የተጠሩት ግን የተገባቸው አልነበሩም።
am.B: ከዚያም ባሪያዎቹን እንዲህ አላቸው፦ “ሰርጉ ተዘጋጅቷል፤ የጋበዝኳቸው እንግዶች ግን ለመምጣት የሚገባቸው አልነበሩም።
am.R: ከዚያም ንጉሡ ባሪያዎቹን እንዲህ አላቸው፦ “የሰርጉ ድግስ ተዘጋጅቷል። የጋበዝኳቸው ሰዎች ግን ሊመጡ አይገባቸውም ነበር።

decisions.choice: not worthy: they showed themselves unfit by refusing
decisions.reason: Their refusal and violence proved them unworthy of the honor (compare 10:11-13).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dice); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (dijo)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells parts of this passage in the present. Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same in verses 12, 16, 20 and 21.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anawaambia); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Matthew tells parts of this passage in the present. Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same in verses 12, 16, 20 and 21.

decisions.choice: Present "말한다" (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew's present tense of narration at Literal.

decisions.choice: "vua nói" (L) with no "đã"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Matthew's present of narration by leaving out the past marker (also 22:12, 22:16, 22:20-21).

source.text: πορεύεσθε οὖν ἐπὶ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὁδῶν, καὶ ὅσους ἐὰν εὕρητε καλέσατε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.

records.literal_gloss: Go therefore to the thoroughfares of the highways, and as many as you find invite to the wedding feast.

en.L: Go therefore to the outlets of the roads, and as many as you find, invite to the wedding feast.'
en.B: So go out to where the roads leave the city, and invite to the wedding anyone you come across.'
en.R: So go out to the main roads. Invite everyone you find to come to the wedding party.'

es.L: {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}}, pues, a los extremos de los caminos, y a cuantos {{plural_you:encuentren|encontréis}}, {{plural_you:invítenlos|invitadlos}} a la fiesta de bodas”.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:vayan|id}} a donde los caminos salen de la ciudad, e {{plural_you:inviten|invitad}} a la boda a todos los que {{plural_you:encuentren|encontréis}}”.
es.R: Por eso, {{plural_you:vayan|id}} a los caminos principales. {{plural_you:Inviten|Invitad}} a la fiesta de bodas a todas las personas que {{plural_you:encuentren|encontréis}}”.

fr.L: Allez donc aux issues des chemins, et tous ceux que vous trouverez, invitez-les aux noces.”
fr.B: Allez donc là où les chemins sortent de la ville, et invitez aux noces tous ceux que vous rencontrerez.”
fr.R: Allez donc sur les grandes routes. Invitez à la fête de mariage tous les gens que vous trouverez.”

sw.L: Basi nendeni kwenye miisho ya njia, na wote mtakaowakuta, waalikeni kwenye karamu ya arusi.'
sw.B: Basi nendeni mahali njia zinapotoka mjini, mkamwalike arusini kila mtu mtakayemkuta.'
sw.R: Basi nendeni kwenye barabara kuu. Mwalikeni kila mtu mtakayemkuta aje kwenye sherehe ya arusi.'

vi.L: Vậy hãy đi ra các ngã đường, và hễ gặp ai, hãy mời đến dự tiệc cưới.'
vi.B: Vậy các ngươi hãy ra những nơi đường phố dẫn ra khỏi thành, gặp ai thì mời người ấy đến dự tiệc cưới.'
vi.R: Vậy các ngươi hãy ra những con đường lớn. Gặp ai thì mời người ấy đến dự tiệc cưới.'

ko.L: 그러므로 너희는 길들이 [성 밖으로] 나가는 곳으로 가서, 만나는 사람은 누구든지 혼인 잔치에 불러라.'
ko.B: 그러니 너희는 길들이 성 밖으로 이어지는 큰길 어귀로 나가서, 만나는 사람은 누구든지 혼인 잔치에 초대하여라.'
ko.R: 그러니 너희는 큰길로 나가거라. 거기서 만나는 사람은 누구든지 결혼 잔치에 오라고 하여라.'

pt.L: Vão, pois, às saídas dos caminhos, e todos quantos encontrarem, convidem para a festa de casamento.'
pt.B: Vão, então, aos lugares onde as estradas saem da cidade, e convidem para o casamento todos os que encontrarem.'
pt.R: Então vão até as estradas principais. Convidem todas as pessoas que vocês encontrarem para virem à festa de casamento.'

am.L: እንግዲህ ወደ መንገዶች መውጫ ሂዱ፤ ያገኛችሁትንም ሁሉ ወደ ሰርጉ ጥሩ።”
am.B: ስለዚህ መንገዶቹ ከከተማ ወደሚወጡበት ሂዱ፤ ያገኛችሁትንም ሁሉ ወደ ሰርጉ ጋብዙ።”
am.R: ስለዚህ ወደ ዋና ዋና መንገዶች ሂዱ። ያገኛችሁትን ሰው ሁሉ ወደ ሰርጉ ድግስ እንዲመጣ ጋብዙ።”

decisions.choice: the outlets of the roads: where the city streets run out into the country roads
alternatives: the main crossroads in the city
decisions.reason: The word names a way out or a place where roads branch. Either way, it is where many travelers would be found.

decisions.choice: as many as you find: an invitation open to all
decisions.reason: The king no longer asks who the guests are. The parable echoes 8:11, where many come from east and west.

decisions.choice: where the roads leave the city
decisions.reason: Balanced says plainly what the phrase describes.

decisions.choice: aux issues des chemins (L)
decisions.reason: The word names the points where the city streets run out into the country roads (m1), the way out of the city, not a crossroads; "issues" keeps that sense at Literal.

decisions.choice: miisho ya njia (the ends of the roads)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the place where a street runs out of the city into the open road (meaning decision m1, uncertain). "Njia panda" would mean a crossroads, which is a different place.

decisions.choice: "길들이 [성 밖으로] 나가는 곳" (L); "큰길 어귀" (B); "큰길" (R)
decisions.reason: The place where the city streets run out into the country roads (meaning decision); Literal brackets the words Korean needs to say it.

decisions.choice: "các ngã đường" (L); "những nơi đường phố dẫn ra khỏi thành" (B)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision places them where the city streets run out into the country roads; Literal keeps a short phrase, Balanced says where it was, as the English Balanced does. "các ngươi" is the king's word for his servants.

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς συνήγαγον πάντας οὓς εὗρον, πονηρούς τε καὶ ἀγαθούς· καὶ ἐπλήσθη ὁ γάμος ἀνακειμένων.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out, those slaves into the highways gathered all whom they found, both evil and good; and was filled the wedding feast with those reclining.

en.L: And those slaves went out into the roads and gathered all whom they found, both evil and good; and the wedding feast was filled with those reclining [at table].
en.B: The servants went out into the streets and brought in everyone they could find, bad and good alike, and the wedding feast was crowded with guests.
en.R: So the servants went out into the roads. They brought in all the people they could find, both bad people and good people. Soon the wedding party was full of guests.

es.L: Y saliendo aquellos esclavos a los caminos, reunieron a todos los que encontraron, tanto malos como buenos; y la fiesta de bodas se llenó de los que se reclinaban [a la mesa].
es.B: Los siervos salieron a los caminos y reunieron a todos los que encontraron, malos y buenos por igual, y el banquete de bodas se llenó de invitados.
es.R: Los siervos salieron a los caminos. Trajeron a toda la gente que encontraron, tanto a los malos como a los buenos. Pronto la fiesta de bodas estuvo llena de invitados.

fr.L: Et ces esclaves, étant sortis sur les chemins, ont rassemblé tous ceux qu’ils ont trouvés, mauvais et bons ; et le festin de noces a été rempli de [convives] étendus [à table].
fr.B: Les serviteurs sont sortis dans les rues et ont rassemblé tous ceux qu’ils ont trouvés, les mauvais comme les bons, et la foule des invités a rempli le banquet de noces.
fr.R: Alors les serviteurs sont allés sur les routes. Ils ont fait venir tous les gens qu’ils ont trouvés, les méchants comme les bons. Bientôt, la fête de mariage a été pleine d’invités.

sw.L: Na watumwa wale, wakitoka kwenda barabarani, waliwakusanya wote waliowakuta, waovu na wema pia; na karamu ya arusi ikajaa walioegemea [mezani].
sw.B: Watumishi hao walitoka, wakaenda barabarani, wakawakusanya wote waliowakuta, wabaya na wema pia. Basi karamu ya arusi ikajaa watu walioketi kula.
sw.R: Basi watumishi walitoka, wakaenda barabarani. Waliwaleta watu wote waliowakuta, watu wabaya na watu wema. Muda si mrefu sherehe ya arusi ilikuwa imejaa wageni.

vi.L: Và các nô lệ ấy đi ra các đường, tập hợp tất cả những người họ gặp, cả kẻ xấu lẫn người tốt; và tiệc cưới đầy những người ngồi [dự tiệc].
vi.B: Các đầy tớ ấy đi ra đường phố và đưa về hết những người họ gặp, cả xấu lẫn tốt, và phòng tiệc cưới đông chật khách.
vi.R: Vậy các đầy tớ đi ra những con đường. Họ đưa về tất cả những người họ gặp, cả người xấu lẫn người tốt. Chẳng bao lâu, tiệc cưới đầy khách.

ko.L: 그리고 그 종들이 길로 나가서, 만나는 사람들을 악한 사람이든 선한 사람이든 모두 모아들였다. 그리고 혼인 잔치는 [식탁에] 기대어 앉은 사람들로 가득 찼다.
ko.B: 종들은 길거리로 나가서, 악한 사람이든 선한 사람이든 만나는 대로 모두 데려왔다. 그래서 혼인 잔치 자리는 손님들로 가득 찼다.
ko.R: 그래서 종들은 큰길로 나가서 만나는 사람들을 모두 데려왔다. 나쁜 사람도 있었고 착한 사람도 있었다. 결혼 잔치 자리는 곧 손님들로 꽉 찼다.

pt.L: E aqueles escravos saíram pelos caminhos e reuniram todos os que encontraram, tanto maus quanto bons; e a festa de casamento se encheu de [pessoas] reclinadas [à mesa].
pt.B: Os servos saíram pelas ruas e trouxeram todos os que conseguiram encontrar, maus e bons, e a festa de casamento ficou cheia de convidados.
pt.R: Então os servos foram para as estradas. Trouxeram todas as pessoas que conseguiram encontrar, tanto pessoas más como pessoas boas. Logo a festa de casamento ficou cheia de convidados.

am.L: እነዚያም ባሪያዎች ወደ መንገዶች ወጥተው ክፉዎችንም ደጎችንም ያገኙትን ሁሉ ሰበሰቡ፤ ሰርጉም [በማዕድ] በተቀመጡ ሞላ።
am.B: ባሪያዎቹም ወደ መንገዶቹ ወጥተው ክፉዎችንም ደጎችንም ያገኙትን ሁሉ ሰበሰቡ፤ የሰርጉም አዳራሽ በእንግዶች ተሞላ።
am.R: ስለዚህ ባሪያዎቹ ወደ መንገዶቹ ወጡ። ያገኟቸውን ሰዎች ሁሉ፣ መጥፎ ሰዎችንም ጥሩ ሰዎችንም አመጡ። ብዙም ሳይቆይ የሰርጉ ድግስ በእንግዶች ሞላ።

decisions.choice: evil and good: the invitation goes to all, whatever their lives
decisions.reason: Bad and good are gathered alike. The sorting comes later, as in the net of 13:47-48 and here in 22:11-13.

decisions.choice: reclining: guests at a feast lay on couches around the table
decisions.reason: As in 8:11 and 9:10, guests at a banquet reclined.

decisions.choice: the wedding feast, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the wedding hall, the reading of other manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "the wedding hall" here. The sense is the same: the place of the feast was full. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: "[식탁에] 기대어 앉은" (L); "손님들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a feast (meaning decision); Literal keeps the picture, Balanced and Readable say "guests".

decisions.choice: "những người ngồi [dự tiệc]" (L); "khách" (B, R) for those reclining
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a feast (meaning decision); Vietnamese "nằm" would suggest sleeping, so Literal says they were at table and Balanced and Readable say "guests".

source.text: εἰσελθὼν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς θεάσασθαι τοὺς ἀνακειμένους εἶδεν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἐνδεδυμένον ἔνδυμα γάμου·

records.literal_gloss: Having entered then the king to see those reclining, he saw there a man not clothed in clothing of wedding;

en.L: But when the king came in to look at those reclining [at table], he saw there a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.
en.B: The king came in to look over his guests, and among them he saw a man who had not put on clothes for a wedding.
en.R: Then the king came in to meet the guests. He saw one man there who was not dressed for a wedding.

es.L: Pero, entrando el rey a ver a los que se reclinaban [a la mesa], vio allí a un hombre que no estaba vestido con ropa de boda.
es.B: Cuando el rey entró a ver a sus invitados, vio entre ellos a un hombre que no se había puesto ropa de boda.
es.R: Luego el rey entró para conocer a los invitados. Allí vio a un hombre que no estaba vestido para una boda.

fr.L: Mais le roi, étant entré pour voir les [convives] étendus [à table], a vu là un homme qui n’était pas vêtu d’un habit de noces.
fr.B: Le roi est entré pour regarder ses invités, et il a vu parmi eux un homme qui n’avait pas mis d’habit de noces.
fr.R: Ensuite, le roi est entré pour rencontrer les invités. Il a vu là un homme qui n’était pas habillé pour un mariage.

sw.L: Lakini mfalme alipoingia kuwatazama walioegemea [mezani], aliona huko mtu ambaye hakuwa amevaa nguo za arusi.
sw.B: Mfalme alipoingia kuwaangalia wageni wake, alimwona mtu mmoja kati yao ambaye hakuwa amevaa mavazi ya arusi.
sw.R: Kisha mfalme aliingia kuonana na wageni. Akamwona mtu mmoja pale ambaye hakuwa amevaa nguo za arusi.

vi.L: Nhưng khi vua vào để xem những khách ngồi [dự tiệc], vua thấy ở đó có một người không mặc áo lễ cưới.
vi.B: Khi vua vào xem các khách dự tiệc, vua thấy trong đó có một người không mặc áo dự tiệc cưới.
vi.R: Rồi vua vào để gặp các khách. Vua thấy có một người không mặc quần áo dành cho đám cưới.

ko.L: 그런데 왕이 [식탁에] 기대어 앉은 사람들을 보려고 들어왔다가, 거기에 혼인 예복을 입지 않은 한 사람을 보았다.
ko.B: 왕이 손님들을 둘러보려고 들어왔다가, 혼인 잔치에 맞는 예복을 입지 않은 사람 하나를 보았다.
ko.R: 왕이 손님들을 만나려고 들어왔다. 그런데 거기에 결혼 잔치에 맞는 옷을 입지 않은 사람이 하나 있었다.

pt.L: Mas, quando o rei entrou para ver os que estavam reclinados [à mesa], viu ali um homem que não estava vestido com roupa de casamento.
pt.B: O rei entrou para ver os convidados e, entre eles, viu um homem que não tinha posto roupa de festa de casamento.
pt.R: Então o rei entrou para cumprimentar os convidados. Ele viu ali um homem que não estava vestido para um casamento.

am.L: ንጉሡም በማዕድ የተቀመጡትን ለማየት በገባ ጊዜ በዚያ የሰርግ ልብስ ያልለበሰ ሰው አየ።
am.B: ንጉሡም እንግዶቹን ለማየት ገባ፤ በመካከላቸውም የሰርግ ልብስ ያልለበሰ አንድ ሰው አየ።
am.R: ከዚያም ንጉሡ እንግዶቹን ሊያገኝ ገባ። በዚያም ለሰርግ የሚገባ ልብስ ያልለበሰ አንድ ሰው አየ።

decisions.choice: wedding clothes: clean, festive clothing fit for the occasion
alternatives: clothing given out by the host
decisions.reason: Guests were expected to come in clean clothes worthy of the feast. Whether the host supplied them is not stated and cannot be shown from the customs of the time.

decisions.choice: the wedding clothes: a life that fits the invitation
alternatives: a righteousness given as a gift
decisions.reason: The parable does not explain the garment. In Matthew the kingdom calls for a righteousness that goes beyond outward show (5:20; 7:21) and for fruit fitting repentance (3:8). Others read it as faith, or as a gift from the host.

decisions.choice: "혼인 예복" (L); "혼인 잔치에 맞는 예복" (B); "결혼 잔치에 맞는 옷" (R)
decisions.reason: Clean, festive clothing fit for the occasion (meaning decision), not a special uniform.

decisions.choice: "áo lễ cưới" (L); "áo dự tiệc cưới" (B); "quần áo dành cho đám cưới" (R)
decisions.reason: "Áo cưới" in Vietnamese is the bride's or groom's dress; the meaning decision describes festive clothing fit for a guest, so each level names a guest's garment.

decisions.choice: "በማዕድ የተቀመጡ" (L) for those reclining
decisions.reason: Guests reclined on couches at a feast; Amharic "የተጋደሙ" would suggest lying down to rest, so Literal says they sat at the table, which is the act meant.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἑταῖρε, πῶς εἰσῆλθες ὧδε μὴ ἔχων ἔνδυμα γάμου;

records.literal_gloss: And he says to him, Friend, how did you enter here not having clothing of wedding?

en.L: And he says to him, 'Friend, how did you come in here without having wedding clothes?'
en.B: He said to him, 'Friend, how is it that you came in here with no wedding clothes on?'
en.R: The king said to him, 'Friend, how did you get in here? You are not dressed for a wedding.'

es.L: Y le dice: “Amigo, ¿cómo entraste aquí sin tener ropa de boda?”.
es.B: Le dijo: “Amigo, ¿cómo es que entraste aquí sin ropa de boda?”.
es.R: El rey le dijo: “Amigo, ¿cómo entraste aquí? No estás vestido para una boda”.

fr.L: Et il lui dit : “Ami, comment es-tu entré ici sans avoir d’habit de noces ?”
fr.B: Il lui a dit : “Mon ami, comment se fait-il que tu sois entré ici sans habit de noces ?”
fr.R: Le roi lui a dit : “Mon ami, comment es-tu entré ici ? Tu n’es pas habillé pour un mariage.”

sw.L: Naye anamwambia, 'Rafiki, ulikujaje ndani hapa bila kuwa na nguo za arusi?'
sw.B: Akamwuliza, 'Rafiki, imekuwaje ukaingia humu bila kuvaa nguo za arusi?'
sw.R: Mfalme akamwambia, 'Rafiki, uliingiaje hapa? Hujavaa nguo za arusi.'

vi.L: Và vua nói với người ấy: 'Này bạn, sao bạn vào đây mà không có áo lễ cưới?'
vi.B: Vua hỏi người ấy: 'Này bạn, sao bạn vào đây mà không mặc áo dự tiệc cưới?'
vi.R: Vua hỏi người ấy: 'Này bạn, làm sao bạn vào được đây? Bạn không mặc quần áo dành cho đám cưới.'

ko.L: 그리고 그에게 말한다. '친구여, 네가 어떻게 혼인 예복도 없이 여기에 들어왔느냐?'
ko.B: 왕이 그에게 말했다. '친구여, 너는 어찌하여 혼인 예복도 입지 않고 여기에 들어왔느냐?'
ko.R: 왕이 그 사람에게 말했다. '친구여, 어떻게 여기에 들어왔느냐? 너는 결혼 잔치에 맞는 옷을 입지 않았구나.'

pt.L: E lhe diz: 'Amigo, como você entrou aqui sem ter roupa de casamento?'
pt.B: Ele lhe disse: 'Amigo, como foi que você entrou aqui sem roupa de casamento?'
pt.R: O rei disse a ele: 'Amigo, como você entrou aqui? Você não está vestido para um casamento.'

am.L: እንዲህም ይለዋል፦ “ወዳጄ ሆይ፣ የሰርግ ልብስ ሳይኖርህ እንዴት ወደዚህ ገባህ?”
am.B: “ወዳጄ፣ የሰርግ ልብስ ሳትለብስ እንዴት ወደዚህ ልትገባ ቻልክ?” አለው።
am.R: ንጉሡም “ወዳጄ፣ እንዴት ወደዚህ ገባህ? ለሰርግ የሚገባ ልብስ አልለበስክም” አለው።

decisions.choice: friend: a polite address, here with a note of reproach
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this address for someone in the wrong: the grumbling worker (20:13) and Judas (26:50).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: a question and a statement
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question to keep the sentences short.

decisions.choice: Ami (L); Mon ami (B, R)
decisions.reason: The address is polite with a note of reproach (m1). French "Mon ami" said to a stranger carries exactly that, and the king says "tu" to one man; Literal keeps the bare vocative.

decisions.choice: "친구여"
decisions.reason: A polite address that carries a note of reproach here (meaning decision); "친구여" is a dignified address that can carry that edge; "여보게" is a reviewer's alternative. The same address comes back in 20:13 and 26:50.

decisions.choice: Present "말한다" (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew's present tense of narration at Literal.

decisions.choice: "Này bạn" and "bạn" for the king's "Friend"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision hears a polite address with a note of reproach; "Này bạn" keeps the courtesy while the question carries the rebuke. The king turns to "ngươi" only for his servants.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἐφιμώθη.

records.literal_gloss: He but was speechless.

en.L: But he was speechless.
en.B: The man had nothing to say.
en.R: The man did not know what to say.

es.L: Pero él se quedó sin habla.
es.B: El hombre no tuvo nada que decir.
es.R: El hombre no supo qué decir.

fr.L: Mais lui est resté muet.
fr.B: L’homme n’a rien eu à répondre.
fr.R: L’homme ne savait pas quoi dire.

sw.L: Lakini yeye alinyamaza kimya.
sw.B: Yule mtu hakuwa na la kusema.
sw.R: Yule mtu hakujua la kusema.

vi.L: Nhưng người ấy lặng thinh.
vi.B: Người ấy không nói được lời nào.
vi.R: Người ấy không biết nói gì.

ko.L: 그러나 그는 말문이 막혔다.
ko.B: 그 사람은 아무 대답도 하지 못했다.
ko.R: 그 사람은 무슨 말을 해야 할지 몰랐다.

pt.L: Mas ele emudeceu.
pt.B: O homem não tinha nada a dizer.
pt.R: O homem não soube o que dizer.

am.L: እርሱ ግን አፉ ተዘጋ።
am.B: ሰውየውም የሚለው አጣ።
am.R: ሰውየውም ምን እንደሚል አላወቀም።

decisions.choice: speechless: silenced, with no excuse to give
decisions.reason: The verb means to be muzzled. The same word is used of the Sadducees in 22:34.

source.text: τότε ὁ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν τοῖς διακόνοις· Δήσαντες αὐτοῦ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ἐκβάλετε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.

records.literal_gloss: Then the king said to the servants, Having bound of him feet and hands, throw out him into the darkness the outer; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.

en.L: Then the king said to the servants, 'Bind his feet and hands and throw him out into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'
en.B: The king then gave orders to his attendants: 'Bind his hands and feet and throw him out into the darkness outside, where people will weep and grind their teeth.'
en.R: Then the king said to his attendants, 'Tie up this man's hands and feet. Throw him outside into the dark. There people will cry and grind their teeth.'

es.L: Entonces el rey dijo a los servidores: “Atándole los pies y las manos, {{plural_you:échenlo|echadlo}} a la oscuridad exterior; allí habrá llanto y rechinar de dientes”.
es.B: Entonces el rey ordenó a los servidores: “{{plural_you:Átenlo|Atadlo}} de pies y manos y {{plural_you:échenlo|echadlo}} fuera, a la oscuridad, donde la gente llorará y rechinará los dientes”.
es.R: Entonces el rey les dijo a los que servían en la fiesta: “{{plural_you:Átenle|Atadle}} las manos y los pies a este hombre. {{plural_you:Échenlo|Echadlo}} afuera, a la oscuridad. Allí la gente llorará y rechinará los dientes”.

fr.L: Alors le roi a dit aux serviteurs : “Lui ayant lié les pieds et les mains, jetez-le dehors, dans les ténèbres du dehors ; là il y aura les pleurs et le grincement des dents.”
fr.B: Alors le roi a donné cet ordre à ceux qui faisaient le service : “Attachez-lui les mains et les pieds et jetez-le dehors, dans l’obscurité, où l’on pleurera et grincera des dents.”
fr.R: Alors le roi a dit aux hommes qui servaient à table : “Attachez les mains et les pieds de cet homme. Jetez-le dehors, dans le noir. Là-bas, les gens vont pleurer et grincer des dents.”

sw.L: Kisha mfalme aliwaambia wahudumu, 'Mkiisha kumfunga miguu na mikono, mtupeni kwenye giza lililo nje; huko kutakuwa na kulia na kusaga meno.'
sw.B: Kisha mfalme akawaamuru wahudumu wake, 'Mfungeni miguu na mikono, mkamtupe nje gizani, ambako watu watalia na kusaga meno.'
sw.R: Kisha mfalme akawaambia wahudumu wake, 'Mfungeni mtu huyu mikono na miguu. Mtupeni nje gizani. Huko watu watalia na kusaga meno.'

vi.L: Bấy giờ vua nói với những người phục vụ: 'Hãy trói chân tay hắn lại và ném hắn ra chỗ tối tăm bên ngoài; ở đó sẽ có khóc lóc và nghiến răng.'
vi.B: Bấy giờ vua ra lệnh cho những người hầu bàn: 'Hãy trói tay chân hắn lại và ném hắn ra chỗ tối tăm bên ngoài, là nơi người ta sẽ khóc lóc và nghiến răng.'
vi.R: Rồi vua nói với những người hầu: 'Hãy trói tay chân người này lại. Hãy ném hắn ra ngoài, vào chỗ tối tăm. Ở đó người ta sẽ khóc lóc và nghiến răng.'

ko.L: 그때에 왕이 시중드는 사람들에게 말했다. '그의 발과 손을 묶어서 그를 바깥의 어둠 속으로 내던져라. 거기에는 울음과 이를 가는 일이 있을 것이다.'
ko.B: 그러자 왕이 시중드는 사람들에게 명령했다. '이 사람의 손발을 묶어서 바깥 어둠 속으로 내던져라. 거기서 그는 울며 이를 갈 것이다.'
ko.R: 그러자 왕이 시중드는 사람들에게 말했다. '이 사람의 손과 발을 꽁꽁 묶어라. 그리고 밖의 어둠 속으로 내던져라. 거기서 사람들은 울며 이를 갈 것이다.'

pt.L: Então o rei disse aos servos: 'Amarrem-lhe os pés e as mãos e lancem-no nas trevas de fora; ali haverá o choro e o ranger de dentes.'
pt.B: Então o rei deu ordens aos seus criados: 'Amarrem as mãos e os pés dele e joguem-no para fora, na escuridão, onde as pessoas vão chorar e ranger os dentes.'
pt.R: Então o rei disse aos seus criados: 'Amarrem as mãos e os pés deste homem. Joguem-no lá fora, no escuro. Lá as pessoas vão chorar e ranger os dentes.'

am.L: በዚያን ጊዜ ንጉሡ አገልጋዮቹን እንዲህ አለ፦ “እግሩንና እጁን አስራችሁ በውጭ ወዳለው ጨለማ አውጡት፤ በዚያ ልቅሶና ጥርስ ማፋጨት ይሆናል።”
am.B: ንጉሡም አገልጋዮቹን እንዲህ ሲል አዘዘ፦ “እጁንና እግሩን አስራችሁ ወደ ውጭ ጨለማ ጣሉት፤ በዚያ ሰዎች ያለቅሳሉ፤ ጥርሳቸውንም ያፋጫሉ።”
am.R: ከዚያም ንጉሡ አገልጋዮቹን እንዲህ አላቸው፦ “የዚህን ሰው እጁንና እግሩን እሰሩ። ወደ ውጭ ወደ ጨለማው ጣሉት። በዚያ ሰዎች ያለቅሳሉ፤ ጥርሳቸውንም ያፋጫሉ።”

decisions.choice: the outer darkness, weeping and gnashing of teeth: exclusion and anguish
alternatives: a literal room outside the hall
decisions.reason: As in 8:12, the darkness outside the lighted hall pictures being shut out of the kingdom, and grinding the teeth shows anguish. The wording is kept the same as in 8:12 at each level.

decisions.choice: servants: attendants who wait at table
alternatives: the same slaves who invited the guests
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the slaves of 22:3-10. In the parable of the weeds, angels carry out the final sorting (13:41-42).

decisions.choice: there will be weeping: the king's words, which also speak of the final judgment
alternatives: a comment by Jesus outside the story
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuation keeps the clause in the king's sentence. The words are Jesus's own phrase for final judgment (8:12; 13:42), so the story and its meaning meet here.

decisions.choice: servants (L); attendants (B, R)
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the one in 22:3-10, which Literal renders "slaves" and Balanced and Readable "servants". To keep the two groups apart, Literal says "servants" here and Balanced and Readable "attendants".

decisions.choice: servidores (L, B); los que servían en la fiesta (R)
decisions.reason: These are not the slaves of verses 3-10 but a different word, for attendants who wait at table (meaning decision m2). "Servidores" keeps them apart from the "siervos"; Readable says what they did, as the English "attendants" does.

decisions.choice: aux serviteurs (L); à ceux qui faisaient le service (B); aux hommes qui servaient à table (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, these attendants are kept apart from the slaves of 22:3-10: Literal calls those "esclaves" and these "serviteurs", while Balanced and Readable, where the others are "serviteurs", describe the table service these men do (m2). "Serveurs" would sound like a restaurant.

decisions.choice: wahudumu
decisions.reason: These are not the slaves of verses 3-10 but a different word, for attendants who wait at table (meaning decision m2). "Wahudumu" are people who serve guests; it keeps them apart from the "watumishi".

decisions.choice: "시중드는 사람들" for diakonoi
decisions.reason: These are attendants who wait at table, a different word from the slaves sent out with the invitations (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "바깥의 어둠... 울음과 이를 가는 일" (L); "바깥 어둠... 울며 이를 갈 것이다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same words as the Korean Matthew 8:12.

decisions.choice: "những người phục vụ" (L); "những người hầu bàn" (B); "những người hầu" (R) for diakonoi
decisions.reason: The Greek changes from slaves to those who wait at table (meaning decision), so Vietnamese uses a different word from "nô lệ"/"đầy tớ".

decisions.choice: "chỗ tối tăm bên ngoài"; "khóc lóc và nghiến răng"
decisions.reason: The wording of Matthew 8:12 and 13:42 at each level, so the reader hears the same warning.

decisions.choice: servos (L); criados (B, R)
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the one in 22:3-10 (m2), which Literal renders "escravos" and Balanced and Readable "servos". To keep the two groups apart, as the English does, Literal says "servos" here and Balanced and Readable "criados", the attendants of a household.

decisions.choice: "አገልጋዮች" (attendants)
decisions.reason: The Greek changes word here, from the slaves who carried the invitation to the attendants who serve at the feast, and Amharic changes word with it.

source.text: πολλοὶ γάρ εἰσιν κλητοὶ ὀλίγοι δὲ ἐκλεκτοί.

records.literal_gloss: Many for are called, few but chosen.

en.L: For many are called, but few [are] chosen."
en.B: For the invited are many, but the chosen are few."
en.R: God invites many people, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses only a few."

es.L: Porque muchos son invitados, pero pocos [son] elegidos».
es.B: Porque los invitados son muchos, pero los elegidos son pocos».
es.R: Dios invita a mucha gente, pero elige solo a unos pocos».

fr.L: Car beaucoup sont appelés, mais peu [sont] choisis. »
fr.B: Car les invités sont nombreux, mais les élus sont peu nombreux. »
fr.R: Dieu invite beaucoup de gens, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’en choisit que quelques-uns. »

sw.L: Kwa kuwa wengi ni walioalikwa, lakini wachache [ni] waliochaguliwa."
sw.B: Kwa maana walioalikwa ni wengi, lakini waliochaguliwa ni wachache."
sw.R: Mungu anawaalika watu wengi, lakini anawachagua wachache tu."

vi.L: Vì có nhiều người được gọi, nhưng ít người được chọn."
vi.B: Vì người được mời thì nhiều, nhưng người được chọn thì ít."
vi.R: Vì Đức Chúa Trời mời nhiều người, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chỉ chọn một số ít."

ko.L: 부름받은 사람은 많으나, 택함받은 사람은 적기 때문이다."
ko.B: 초대받은 사람은 많지만, 택함받은 사람은 적다."
ko.R: 하나님께서는 많은 사람을 부르시지만, 그 가운데 적은 사람만 택하신다."

pt.L: Pois muitos são chamados, mas poucos [são] escolhidos."
pt.B: Pois os convidados são muitos, mas os escolhidos são poucos."
pt.R: Deus convida muitas pessoas, mas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} escolhe só algumas."

am.L: ብዙዎች ተጠርተዋልና፣ የተመረጡት ግን ጥቂቶች ናቸው።»
am.B: የተጠሩት ብዙዎች፣ የተመረጡት ግን ጥቂቶች ናቸውና።»
am.R: እግዚአብሔር ብዙ ሰዎችን ይጋብዛል፤ የሚመርጠው ግን ጥቂቶችን ብቻ ነው።»

decisions.choice: called: invited
decisions.reason: The word comes from the same root as "invited" in 22:3-9. Many receive the king's invitation.

decisions.choice: chosen: those whom God accepts at the feast
decisions.reason: The saying sums up the parable. Many were invited, yet the first guests refused and one guest was thrown out. The chosen are those who come and are found fit, by God's choice.

decisions.choice: God invites; he chooses
alternatives: many are called, few are chosen
decisions.reason: The passive words imply that God is the one who calls and chooses. Readable says so.

decisions.choice: the invited are many, the chosen are few
alternatives: many are invited, few are chosen
decisions.reason: Balanced sets the two groups side by side as the Greek does, with the numbers last for emphasis.

decisions.choice: invitados
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one used for the guests "invited" in verses 3, 4 and 8 (meaning decision m1). "Invitados" keeps the saying tied to the story; "llamados" would lose the link.

decisions.choice: walioalikwa
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one used for the guests "invited" in verses 3, 4 and 8 (meaning decision m1). "Walioalikwa" keeps the saying tied to the story; "walioitwa" would lose the link.

decisions.choice: "부름받은" (L), "초대받은" (B); "택함받은" (L, B); God named at Readable
decisions.reason: The word is the same as the invited guests of the story (meaning decision); Balanced says "초대받은" to keep that link, and Readable names God as the one who calls, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "được gọi" (L); "được mời" (B); "Đức Chúa Trời mời" (R) for "called"; "được chọn"
decisions.reason: "Called" here means invited (meaning decision), which ties the saying to the feast; Literal keeps the Greek verb "gọi" and Balanced the sense "mời". Readable names God as the one who invites and chooses, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Τότε πορευθέντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ὅπως αὐτὸν παγιδεύσωσιν ἐν λόγῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Then having gone, the Pharisees took counsel how him they might trap in a word.

en.L: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in [what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said].
en.B: Then the Pharisees went off and plotted how they could catch Jesus out by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own words.
en.R: Then the Pharisees went away and made plans. They wanted to trick Jesus into saying something wrong.

es.L: Entonces los fariseos fueron y tomaron consejo sobre cómo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} atraparían en [lo que dijera].
es.B: Entonces los fariseos se retiraron y tramaron cómo hacer caer a Jesús con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} propias palabras.
es.R: Entonces los fariseos se fueron e hicieron planes. Querían engañar a Jesús para que dijera algo indebido.

fr.L: Alors les Pharisiens, s’en étant allés, tinrent conseil pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} prendre au piège par [ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dirait].
fr.B: Alors les Pharisiens se retirèrent et se concertèrent pour trouver le moyen de piéger Jésus par {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} propres paroles.
fr.R: Ensuite, les Pharisiens sont partis et ils ont fait des plans. Ils voulaient piéger Jésus en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} faisant dire quelque chose de mal.

sw.L: Kisha Mafarisayo, wakiondoka, walishauriana jinsi wangemnasa kwa neno [alilosema].
sw.B: Kisha Mafarisayo waliondoka, wakapanga njama jinsi ya kumkamata Yesu kwa maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe.
sw.R: Kisha Mafarisayo waliondoka, wakapanga mpango. Walitaka kumdanganya Yesu ili aseme jambo baya.

vi.L: Bấy giờ những người Pha-ri-si đi ra và bàn mưu làm thế nào để gài bẫy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong lời nói.
vi.B: Bấy giờ những người Pha-ri-si đi ra và bàn mưu để bắt lỗi Đức Giê-xu bằng chính lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói.
vi.R: Rồi những người Pha-ri-si bỏ đi và bàn tính với nhau. Họ muốn lừa Đức Giê-xu để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói ra điều gì sai.

ko.L: 그때에 바리새파 사람들이 가서, 어떻게 하면 그분을 말로 올무에 걸리게 할까 의논하였다.
ko.B: 그러자 바리새파 사람들이 물러가서, 어떻게 하면 예수를 말로 책잡을 수 있을까 의논했다.
ko.R: 그러자 바리새파 사람들이 물러가서 계획을 세웠다. 그들은 예수께서 무엇인가 잘못된 말을 하시게 만들어서 꼬투리를 잡으려고 했다.

pt.L: Então os fariseus foram e combinaram como poderiam apanhá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} em [alguma coisa que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dissesse].
pt.B: Então os fariseus saíram e tramaram um jeito de apanhar Jesus nas {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} próprias palavras.
pt.R: Então os fariseus foram embora e fizeram planos. Eles queriam enganar Jesus para que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dissesse alguma coisa errada.

am.L: በዚያን ጊዜ ፈሪሳውያን ሄደው በቃሉ እንዴት እንደሚያጠምዱት ተማከሩ።
am.B: ከዚያም ፈሪሳውያን ሄደው ኢየሱስን በገዛ ቃሉ እንዴት እንደሚያጠምዱት ተመካከሩ።
am.R: ከዚያም ፈሪሳውያን ሄደው ዕቅድ አወጡ። ኢየሱስ ስሕተት የሆነ ነገር እንዲናገር ሊያታልሉት ፈለጉ።

decisions.choice: trap: catch, as a hunter snares an animal
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a snare. They wanted a statement they could use against him.

decisions.choice: took counsel: made a plan together
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 12:14, when the Pharisees plot to destroy Jesus.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns, pronouns before the verb and possessives (lo, sus)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the end of the verb ("atraparlo", "muéstrenme"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: les Pharisiens, les Hérodiens (L, B), capitalised; des partisans de la famille du roi Hérode (R, 22:16)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as in Mark 12:13. Readable explains the Herodians as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yake, wewe)
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("wangemnasa", "mnanijaribu"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This applies to the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "말로 올무에 걸리게 하다" (L); "말로 책잡다" (B); "꼬투리를 잡다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures snaring an animal (meaning decision); Literal keeps the snare, Balanced and Readable use the words of the Korean Mark 12:13.

decisions.choice: "gài bẫy" (L); "bắt lỗi" (B); "lừa" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures a hunter's snare (meaning decision); Literal keeps the picture, as in Mark 12:13, and Balanced and Readable say what they wanted.

source.text: καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ διδάσκεις, καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων·

records.literal_gloss: And they send to him the disciples of them with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, we know that true you are and the way of God in truth you teach, and not it is a care to you about no one, not for you look at face of men;

en.L: And they send their disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with the Herodians, saying, "Teacher, we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are true and teach the way of God in truth, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not care about anyone, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not look at [the] face of {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: They sent their own disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} along with the Herodians. "Teacher," they said, "we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are truthful and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach God's way in keeping with the truth. No one's opinion moves {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not judge people by their rank.
en.R: They sent some of their followers to Jesus, together with some men who supported King Herod's family. They said, "Teacher, we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are honest. We know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach the truth about the way God wants people to live. You are not afraid of anyone, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} treat important people the same as everyone else.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} envían sus discípulos con los herodianos, diciendo: «Maestro, sabemos que eres veraz y enseñas el camino de Dios en verdad, y no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} importa nadie, pues no miras [el] rostro de {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}.
es.B: Le enviaron sus discípulos junto con los herodianos. «Maestro», le dijeron, «sabemos que eres sincero y que enseñas el camino de Dios conforme a la verdad. La opinión de nadie {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hace cambiar, porque no juzgas a la gente por su rango.
es.R: Enviaron a algunos de sus seguidores a ver a Jesús, junto con unos hombres que apoyaban a la familia del rey Herodes. Le dijeron: «Maestro, sabemos que eres honesto. Sabemos que enseñas la verdad sobre cómo quiere Dios que viva la gente. No {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} da miedo nadie, porque tratas a las personas importantes igual que a todos los demás.

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} envoient leurs disciples avec les Hérodiens, disant : « Maître, nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es vrai et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enseignes la voie de Dieu dans la vérité, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} soucies de personne, car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne regardes pas au visage des {{gender:humains|hommes}}.
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} envoyèrent leurs propres disciples, accompagnés des Hérodiens. « Maître, dirent-ils, nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} dis la vérité et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enseignes la voie de Dieu en toute vérité. L’opinion de personne ne {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}influence, car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne juges pas les gens d’après leur rang.
fr.R: Ils ont envoyé à Jésus quelques-uns de leurs disciples, avec des partisans de la famille du roi Hérode. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont dit : « Maître, nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es honnête. Nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enseignes la vérité sur la façon dont Dieu veut que les gens vivent. Tu n’as peur de personne, car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} traites les gens importants comme tous les autres.

sw.L: Na wanawatuma {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} wanafunzi wao pamoja na wafuasi wa Herode, wakisema, "Mwalimu, tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mkweli na unafundisha njia ya Mungu katika kweli, wala humjali mtu yeyote, kwa maana hutazami uso wa watu.
sw.B: Waliwatuma wanafunzi wao {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} pamoja na wafuasi wa Herode. Wakamwambia, "Mwalimu, tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mtu wa kweli, na kwamba unafundisha njia ya Mungu kulingana na kweli. Maoni ya mtu yeyote hayakuyumbishi, kwa sababu huwapimi watu kwa vyeo vyao.
sw.R: Waliwatuma baadhi ya wafuasi wao kwa Yesu, pamoja na watu fulani walioiunga mkono familia ya Mfalme Herode. Wakamwambia, "Mwalimu, tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mwaminifu. Tunajua kwamba unafundisha ukweli kuhusu jinsi Mungu anavyotaka watu waishi. Humwogopi mtu yeyote, kwa sababu unawatendea watu wakubwa sawa na watu wengine wote.

vi.L: Và họ sai các môn đồ của mình cùng với những người thuộc phe Hê-rốt đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nói rằng: "Thưa Thầy, chúng tôi biết Thầy là người chân thật và dạy đường lối của Đức Chúa Trời theo chân lý, và Thầy không nể ai cả, vì Thầy không nhìn mặt người ta.
vi.B: Họ sai các môn đồ của mình cùng với những người thuộc phe Hê-rốt đến gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ nói: "Thưa Thầy, chúng tôi biết Thầy là người ngay thật và dạy đường lối của Đức Chúa Trời theo đúng chân lý. Thầy không để ai chi phối mình, vì Thầy không xét người theo địa vị.
vi.R: Họ sai mấy người môn đồ của mình cùng với mấy người ủng hộ gia đình vua Hê-rốt đến gặp Đức Giê-xu. Họ nói: "Thưa Thầy, chúng tôi biết Thầy là người thật thà. Thầy dạy sự thật về cách Đức Chúa Trời muốn người ta sống. Thầy không sợ ai cả, vì Thầy đối xử với người quan trọng cũng như với mọi người khác.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 자기 제자들을 헤롯 당원들과 함께 그분께 보내며 말한다. "선생님, 저희는 선생님께서 참되시고, 하나님의 길을 진리 안에서 가르치시며, 아무에게도 마음을 쓰지 않으신다는 것을 압니다. 선생님께서는 사람들의 얼굴을 보지 않으시기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그들은 자기 제자들을 헤롯 당원들과 함께 예수께 보냈다. 그들이 말했다. "선생님, 저희는 선생님께서 진실하신 분이시고, 하나님의 길을 참되게 가르치시며, 아무에게도 휘둘리지 않으신다는 것을 압니다. 선생님께서는 사람의 지위를 따지지 않으십니다.
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들은 자기 제자들을 예수께 보냈다. 헤롯 왕의 집안을 따르는 사람들도 함께 보냈다. 그들이 말했다. "선생님, 저희는 선생님께서 정직하신 분이라는 것을 압니다. 선생님께서는 하나님께서 원하시는 삶의 길을 참되게 가르치십니다. 선생님께서는 아무도 두려워하지 않으십니다. 높은 사람이든 낮은 사람이든 똑같이 대하십니다.

pt.L: E enviam a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os seus discípulos com os herodianos, dizendo: "Mestre, sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és sincero e ensinas na verdade o caminho de Deus, e não {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} preocupas com ninguém, pois não olhas para o rosto {{gender:das pessoas|dos homens}}.
pt.B: Mandaram até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os seus próprios discípulos, junto com os herodianos. "Mestre", disseram, "sabemos que és sincero e que ensinas o caminho de Deus de acordo com a verdade. A opinião dos outros não {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} influencia, porque não julgas as pessoas pela posição que ocupam.
pt.R: Eles mandaram alguns dos seus seguidores até Jesus, junto com alguns homens que apoiavam a família do rei Herodes. Eles disseram: "Mestre, sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és honesto. Sabemos que ensinas a verdade sobre o jeito como Deus quer que as pessoas vivam. Tu não tens medo de ninguém, porque tratas as pessoas importantes do mesmo jeito que todas as outras.

am.L: ደቀ መዛሙርታቸውንም ከሄሮድስ ወገኖች ጋር ወደ እርሱ ይልካሉ፤ እንዲህም እያሉ፦ «መምህር ሆይ፣ እውነተኛ እንደ ሆንህ፣ የእግዚአብሔርንም መንገድ በእውነት እንደምታስተምር፣ ለማንም ግድ እንደሌለህም እናውቃለን፤ የሰዎችን ፊት አትመለከትምና።
am.B: ደቀ መዛሙርታቸውን ከሄሮድስ ወገኖች ጋር ወደ እርሱ ላኩ። «መምህር ሆይ» አሉት፤ «አንተ እውነተኛ እንደ ሆንህና የእግዚአብሔርን መንገድ በእውነት እንደምታስተምር እናውቃለን። የማንም ሰው አስተያየት አያንቀሳቅስህም፤ ሰዎችን በማዕረጋቸው አታዳላምና።
am.R: ከዚያም ከደቀ መዛሙርታቸው አንዳንዶቹን የንጉሥ ሄሮድስን ቤተሰብ ከሚደግፉ ሰዎች ጋር ወደ ኢየሱስ ላኩ። እነርሱም እንዲህ አሉ፦ «መምህር ሆይ፣ አንተ ሐቀኛ እንደ ሆንህ እናውቃለን። እግዚአብሔር ሰዎች እንዴት እንዲኖሩ እንደሚፈልግ እውነቱን እንደምታስተምርም እናውቃለን። ማንንም አትፈራም፤ ታላላቅ ሰዎችን እንደ ሌላው ሰው ታያለህና።

decisions.choice: the Herodians: supporters of Herod's family, who ruled under Rome
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas ruled Galilee with Rome's approval. His supporters would favor the tax; many Pharisees resented it. The two groups were unlikely allies (Mark 3:6).

decisions.choice: look at the face of men: show favor because of a person's rank or appearance
decisions.reason: The law forbids judging by a person's standing (Leviticus 19:15; Deuteronomy 1:17). They praise Jesus for fearing no one, hoping he will answer rashly.

decisions.choice: true, in truth: honest, teaching what is really God's way
decisions.reason: Their words are flattery meant to set a trap (22:15, 18), yet what they say about Jesus is so.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: men who supported King Herod's family; the truth about the way God wants people to live
alternatives: the Herodians; the way of God in truth
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Herodians were and what "the way of God" means.

decisions.choice: truthful (B); honest (R)
decisions.reason: The adjective describes a person who speaks the truth. The noun "truth" later in the verse stays "truth" at every level.

decisions.choice: Maître; disciples at every level
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:14: "Maître" is how French addresses a respected teacher, used for this address throughout the chapter. French keeps "disciples" at Readable, where English says "followers", as Mark's French does.

decisions.choice: wafuasi wa Herode (supporters of Herod)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of the Herodians (meaning decision m1). Swahili has no established word for the party, and "Maherodi" would read as several men named Herod.

decisions.choice: The questioners speak to Jesus in full 합쇼체 with honorifics, "저희" and "선생님" for "you", through 22:17
decisions.reason: Their flattery is the trap: they speak with full courtesy, as in the Korean Mark 12:14.

decisions.choice: "헤롯 당원들" (L, B), "헤롯 왕의 집안을 따르는 사람들" (R); "사람들의 얼굴을 보지 않다" (L), "사람의 지위를 따지지 않다" (B)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 12:13-14; Literal keeps the idiom of the face, which means showing favour by rank (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Present "보내며 말한다" (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew's present tense of narration at Literal.

decisions.choice: "Thưa Thầy" and "Thầy" for "you" in the questioners' words, with no deity_pronoun span (22:16-17); "chúng tôi" for themselves
